ICT-18.notes:
> **Why it matters:** Exams ask the three cloud service models (IaaS, PaaS, SaaS) with examples, the deployment models, who coined "Internet of Things", and the Vs of big data. These topics appear in bank IT papers and recent BCS questions.

## Cloud computing (ক্লাউড কম্পিউটিং) 🔥
- **Delivering computing services — servers, storage, databases, software — over the internet, on demand, and paying only for what you use.**
- The idea of computing as a public utility is credited to **John McCarthy** (1961), who is often called the **father of cloud computing** in exam guides.
- Big providers: **Amazon Web Services (AWS, 2006)**, **Microsoft Azure**, **Google Cloud**, IBM Cloud, Alibaba Cloud.

### Key characteristics (NIST)
**On-demand self-service**, **broad network access**, **resource pooling**, **rapid elasticity (scaling up/down)**, **measured service (pay-as-you-go)**.

### Service models 🔥🔥
| Model | Full form | What you get | Examples |
|---|---|---|---|
| 🔥 **IaaS** | Infrastructure as a Service | Virtual **hardware**: servers, storage, networks | **AWS EC2**, Google Compute Engine, Azure VMs |
| 🔥 **PaaS** | Platform as a Service | A **platform** to build and run apps (OS, runtime, database) | **Google App Engine**, Heroku, Azure App Service |
| 🔥 **SaaS** | Software as a Service | **Ready-to-use software** in a browser | **Gmail, Google Docs, Microsoft 365, Dropbox, Salesforce, Zoom** |

- User control is highest in **IaaS** and lowest in **SaaS**. Memory hook: **I**nfrastructure → **P**latform → **S**oftware (bottom to top).

### Deployment models
| Model | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **Public cloud** | Shared by the general public; run by a provider (AWS, Azure) |
| **Private cloud** | Used by **one organisation** only; more control and security |
| **Hybrid cloud** | **Mix of public and private** |
| **Community cloud** | Shared by organisations with common needs (e.g. banks, government bodies) |

- **Advantages:** lower cost, no hardware to maintain, access from anywhere, easy scaling, automatic backup. **Disadvantages:** needs internet, data privacy/security concerns, dependence on the provider.
- **Virtualization** (running many virtual machines on one physical machine) is the **core technology behind cloud**.
- **Edge / fog computing:** processing data **near the source** (device) instead of a far cloud, for low delay.
- Bangladesh: the **National Data Centre** (Tier IV) at the **Hi-Tech Park, Kaliakair, Gazipur**, run by BDCCL, hosts government cloud services.

## Internet of Things (IoT) 🔥
- A network of **physical objects ("things") with sensors, software and connectivity** that collect and exchange data over the internet **without human help**.
- 🔥 The term **"Internet of Things"** was coined by **Kevin Ashton** in **1999**.
- **Components:** **sensors/devices**, **connectivity** (Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, Zigbee, 4G/5G), **data processing (cloud)**, **user interface (app)**.
- **Examples:** **smart home** (smart bulbs, smart locks, Alexa), **smartwatches/fitness bands**, **smart city** (smart traffic lights, smart meters), **smart agriculture** (soil-moisture sensors), connected cars, health monitoring.
- **IIoT** = Industrial IoT (factories, "Industry 4.0").
- IoT is one of the key technologies of the **Fourth Industrial Revolution (4IR)**, a term popularised by **Klaus Schwab** (World Economic Forum, 2016).
- Challenges: security, privacy, power, standards.

## Big data 🔥
- **Extremely large and complex data sets** that normal database software cannot store or process easily.
- Sources: social media, sensors/IoT, online transactions, mobile phones, satellites.
- 🔥 **The 3 Vs** (Doug Laney, 2001): **Volume** (size), **Velocity** (speed of creation), **Variety** (types: structured, semi-structured, unstructured).
- Later added: **Veracity** (accuracy/trust) and **Value** → the **5 Vs**. Some books add Variability and Visualization.

| Data type | Example |
|---|---|
| **Structured** | Tables in a relational database, spreadsheets |
| **Semi-structured** | **XML, JSON**, email |
| **Unstructured** | Images, videos, audio, social media posts (**most big data is unstructured**) |

- **Tools:** 🔥 **Hadoop** (Apache, open source; created by **Doug Cutting** and Mike Cafarella; uses **HDFS** and **MapReduce**), **Apache Spark**, NoSQL databases (**MongoDB**, Cassandra).
- **Data analytics:** examining data to find patterns. **Data mining:** discovering hidden patterns. **Data science** combines statistics, programming and domain knowledge.
- Uses: fraud detection in banks, targeted advertising, weather forecasting, healthcare, traffic, e-commerce recommendations.

## Quick revision
- Cloud = computing services **over the internet, pay-as-you-go**.
- **IaaS** = infrastructure (AWS EC2); **PaaS** = platform (Google App Engine); **SaaS** = software (Gmail, Google Docs).
- Deployment: **public, private, hybrid, community**.
- Core technology of cloud: **virtualization**.
- "Internet of Things" coined by **Kevin Ashton (1999)**.
- Big data 3 Vs: **Volume, Velocity, Variety** (+ Veracity, Value).
- Big data framework: **Hadoop** (HDFS + MapReduce).
- Bangladesh National Data Centre: **Kaliakair, Gazipur** (Tier IV).

ICT-19.notes:
> **Why it matters:** Exams ask the father of AI, the Turing test, types of machine learning, what GPT stands for, which company made ChatGPT/Gemini, and the Sophia robot. Recent BCS and bank papers include AI questions every year.

## Artificial Intelligence (কৃত্রিম বুদ্ধিমত্তা) 🔥
- **AI** is the ability of machines to do tasks that normally need **human intelligence**: learning, reasoning, problem-solving, understanding language, recognising images.
- 🔥 **John McCarthy** coined the term **"Artificial Intelligence"** (1955 proposal) for the **Dartmouth Conference (1956)**. He is the **father of AI** and also created the **LISP** language.
- 🔥 **Alan Turing** proposed the **Turing Test** in his 1950 paper *"Computing Machinery and Intelligence"*: if a human cannot tell a machine from a human in conversation, the machine is "intelligent".
- **Types by capability:** **Narrow/weak AI** (one task, e.g. voice assistants — all AI today), **General AI (AGI)** (human-level in all tasks, not yet achieved), **Super AI** (beyond humans, hypothetical).

### Branches of AI
| Branch | Meaning / example |
|---|---|
| **Machine learning (ML)** | Learning from data without explicit programming |
| **Deep learning** | ML with **multi-layer artificial neural networks** |
| **NLP** (Natural Language Processing) | Understanding human language: translation, chatbots |
| **Computer vision** | Understanding images/video: face recognition |
| **Expert system** | Copies a human expert's decisions using rules (**MYCIN** for medicine, DENDRAL for chemistry) |
| **Robotics** | Machines that sense and act |
| **Speech recognition** | Siri (Apple), Alexa (Amazon), Google Assistant |

### AI milestones 🔥
| Year | Event |
|---|---|
| 1966 | **ELIZA**, first chatbot (Joseph Weizenbaum, MIT) |
| 🔥 1997 | IBM's **Deep Blue** beat world chess champion **Garry Kasparov** |
| 2011 | IBM **Watson** won the quiz show *Jeopardy!* |
| 🔥 2016 | Google DeepMind's **AlphaGo** beat Go champion **Lee Sedol** |
| 2017 | Google researchers introduced the **Transformer** ("Attention Is All You Need") |
| 🔥 **30 Nov 2022** | **OpenAI** released **ChatGPT** |
| 2024 | **Nobel Prize in Physics** to **John Hopfield and Geoffrey Hinton** for neural-network work; **Chemistry** share to **Demis Hassabis and John Jumper** (DeepMind, **AlphaFold**) and David Baker |

## Machine learning (মেশিন লার্নিং) 🔥
- Term coined by **Arthur Samuel** (IBM) in **1959**.

| Type | How it learns | Example |
|---|---|---|
| 🔥 **Supervised learning** | From **labelled data** (input + correct answer) | Spam filter, loan-default prediction, image classification |
| 🔥 **Unsupervised learning** | From **unlabelled data**; finds patterns/groups (**clustering**) | Customer segmentation |
| 🔥 **Reinforcement learning** | By **trial and error with rewards/penalties** | Game-playing AI (AlphaGo), robots, self-driving |

- **Neural network:** a model inspired by the **human brain's neurons**. **Geoffrey Hinton** is called the **"godfather of deep learning/AI"**.
- **Training data** teaches the model; **test data** checks it. **Overfitting** = model memorises training data and fails on new data.

## Large language models (LLMs) and generative AI 🔥
- An **LLM** is a deep-learning model trained on **huge amounts of text** to understand and generate language. Most are built on the **Transformer** architecture.
- 🔥 **GPT = Generative Pre-trained Transformer.**
- **Generative AI** creates new content: text, images, audio, video, code.
- **Prompt:** the instruction given to an AI. **Token:** a small piece of text the model processes. **Hallucination:** when an AI confidently gives false information.

| AI system | Company |
|---|---|
| 🔥 **ChatGPT** (GPT models), DALL·E, Sora | **OpenAI** (USA) |
| **Gemini** (earlier named **Bard**) | **Google** |
| **Claude** | **Anthropic** |
| **Llama** | **Meta** |
| **Copilot** | **Microsoft** |
| **Grok** | **xAI** (Elon Musk) |
| **DeepSeek** | DeepSeek (China) |
| Midjourney, Stable Diffusion | Image generators |

> 🔄 Update: AI models and versions change every few months; check the latest news before the exam.

## Robotics (রোবটিক্স) 🔥
- 🔥 The word **"robot"** comes from the Czech word **"robota" (forced labour)**, first used in **Karel Čapek**'s play ***R.U.R.*** (1920).
- The word **"robotics"** was first used by **Isaac Asimov** (1941), who also gave the **Three Laws of Robotics**.
- **Joseph Engelberger** is called the **father of industrial robotics**; **Unimate** (1961, used by General Motors) was the **first industrial robot**.
- 🔥 **Sophia** is a humanoid robot made by **Hanson Robotics** (Hong Kong; David Hanson). In **2017** it became the **first robot to be given citizenship** (by **Saudi Arabia**). Sophia visited **Dhaka** in **December 2017** for the Digital World event.
- Main parts of a robot: **sensors** (input), **controller** (brain), **actuators** (motors that move), power supply.
- Uses: manufacturing (car assembly), surgery (**da Vinci surgical robot**), space exploration (Mars rovers), defence, bomb disposal, household (robot vacuum).
- **Drone (UAV — Unmanned Aerial Vehicle):** a flying robot.

## Quick revision
- Father of AI: **John McCarthy** (Dartmouth, 1956).
- Turing Test: **Alan Turing (1950)**.
- "Machine learning" coined by **Arthur Samuel (1959)**.
- ML types: **supervised (labelled), unsupervised (clustering), reinforcement (rewards)**.
- GPT = **Generative Pre-trained Transformer**; ChatGPT by **OpenAI (Nov 2022)**.
- Gemini = Google; Claude = Anthropic; Llama = Meta; Copilot = Microsoft.
- Deep Blue beat Kasparov (**1997**); AlphaGo beat Lee Sedol (**2016**).
- "Robot" from Czech **robota**, Karel Čapek; "robotics" from **Isaac Asimov**.
- Sophia: first robot citizen, **Saudi Arabia, 2017**.

ICT-20.notes:
> **Why it matters:** Exams ask who created Bitcoin, what a blockchain is, the difference between VR and AR, and where the word "metaverse" came from. Bank exams also ask about Bangladesh Bank's position on cryptocurrency.

## Blockchain (ব্লকচেইন) 🔥
- A **decentralised, distributed digital ledger** that records transactions in **blocks** linked together in a **chain** using **cryptographic hashes**.
- Each block holds: transaction data, a **timestamp**, its own **hash** and the **hash of the previous block**. Changing one block breaks the chain, so records are practically **immutable (tamper-proof)**.
- Copies of the ledger are kept on many computers (**nodes**) in a **peer-to-peer** network; there is **no central authority**.
- **Consensus mechanisms** (how nodes agree):
  - 🔥 **Proof of Work (PoW):** miners solve hard puzzles — **Bitcoin**.
  - **Proof of Stake (PoS):** validators lock up (stake) coins — **Ethereum** (switched in **2022**, "The Merge").
- **Types:** **public** (Bitcoin, Ethereum), **private** (one organisation), **consortium/federated** (a group of banks), hybrid.
- 🔥 **Smart contract:** a self-executing program on a blockchain that runs automatically when conditions are met. The idea came from **Nick Szabo** (1994); **Ethereum** made it popular.
- **Uses beyond crypto:** land records, supply chain tracking, trade finance, digital identity, voting, healthcare records.

## Cryptocurrency (ক্রিপ্টোকারেন্সি) 🔥
- **Digital money** secured by cryptography and usually run on a blockchain; not issued by any central bank.

| Fact | Detail |
|---|---|
| 🔥 **Bitcoin (BTC)** | **First cryptocurrency**. Created by **"Satoshi Nakamoto"** (pseudonym; real identity unknown). White paper **2008**; network launched **January 2009** |
| Bitcoin supply limit | **21 million** coins |
| Smallest unit of Bitcoin | **Satoshi** = 0.00000001 BTC (10⁻⁸) |
| 🔥 **Ethereum (ETH / Ether)** | **Vitalik Buterin**; launched **2015**; smart contracts |
| Other coins | Tether (USDT, a **stablecoin**), BNB, Solana, Ripple (XRP), Dogecoin |
| **Mining** | Verifying transactions and adding blocks, for a reward |
| **Crypto wallet** | Stores the private keys; **hot wallet** (online) or **cold wallet** (offline) |
| **Altcoin** | Any crypto other than Bitcoin |
| **First country to make Bitcoin legal tender** | **El Salvador** (September 2021) |

- **NFT (Non-Fungible Token):** a unique digital token on a blockchain showing ownership of a digital item (art, music). "Non-fungible" = cannot be swapped one-for-one.
- **CBDC (Central Bank Digital Currency):** digital money **issued by a central bank** (e.g. China's e-CNY, India's e-Rupee). It is **not** a cryptocurrency, because it is centralised.
- 🔥 **Bangladesh:** Bangladesh Bank has repeatedly warned that transactions in cryptocurrencies such as Bitcoin are **not authorised/legal tender** in Bangladesh and may break foreign-exchange and anti-money-laundering laws.

> 🔄 Update: rules on crypto change; check the latest Bangladesh Bank circulars.

## Virtual reality, augmented reality, mixed reality 🔥
| Term | Meaning | Examples |
|---|---|---|

- **Facebook** changed its company name to **Meta Platforms** in **October 2021** to focus on the metaverse.
- Examples of virtual worlds: Second Life, Roblox, Decentraland, Fortnite events.
- **Avatar:** a user's digital character. **Digital twin:** a virtual copy of a real object or system.
- **Web3:** idea of a decentralised internet built on blockchain.

ICT-22.notes:
> **Why it matters:** Exams ask the types of e-commerce (B2B, B2C, C2C), examples of each, the meaning of G2C/G2B, and Bangladesh's e-governance services such as Union Digital Centres, 999, 333 and e-GP. Bank exams add digital payment systems (BEFTN, RTGS, MFS).

## E-commerce (ই-কমার্স) 🔥
- **Buying and selling goods and services over the internet** (electronic commerce).
- **M-commerce:** e-commerce through **mobile phones**. **F-commerce:** selling through **Facebook** pages (very common in Bangladesh). **S-commerce:** social commerce.
- **E-business** is broader: all business activities done electronically (including supply chain, CRM).

### Types of e-commerce 🔥🔥
| Type | Meaning | Example |
|---|---|---|
| 🔥 **B2B** (Business to Business) | Business sells to another business | **Alibaba.com**, wholesale suppliers |
| 🔥 **B2C** (Business to Consumer) | Business sells to individual buyers | **Amazon**, **Daraz**, Chaldal, Rokomari |
| 🔥 **C2C** (Consumer to Consumer) | Individuals sell to each other | **eBay**, **Bikroy.com**, OLX |
| **C2B** (Consumer to Business) | Individuals sell to businesses | Freelancers, stock-photo sellers |
| **B2G** (Business to Government) | Businesses sell to government | Online tenders (e-GP) |

- **Amazon:** founded by **Jeff Bezos** (1994), began as an online bookstore.
- **Alibaba:** founded by **Jack Ma** (1999), China. Alibaba bought **Daraz** in **2018**.
- **eBay:** founded by **Pierre Omidyar** (1995), online auctions.

### Online payment terms
| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **EFT** | Electronic Funds Transfer |
| **Payment gateway** | Service that processes card/online payments for websites (e.g. SSLCOMMERZ in Bangladesh) |
| **COD** | Cash on Delivery — most common payment method in Bangladesh e-commerce |
| **Escrow** | A third party holds the buyer's money until the product is delivered |
| **MFS** (Mobile Financial Service) | **bKash** (BRAC Bank subsidiary, 2011), **Rocket** (Dutch-Bangla Bank, 2011), **Nagad** (Bangladesh Post Office's digital service, 2019) |
| **Digital wallet** | Stores payment information on a phone |

### Bangladesh Bank payment systems 🔥
| System | Full form / job |
|---|---|
| **BACH** | Bangladesh Automated Clearing House: **BACPS** (cheque clearing, 2010) + **BEFTN** (electronic fund transfer, 2011) |
| 🔥 **RTGS** | **Real Time Gross Settlement**: high-value transfers settled instantly, one by one (Bangladesh, **2015**) |
| **NPSB** | National Payment Switch Bangladesh: connects ATMs, POS and internet banking of different banks (2012) |

- In Bangladesh, e-commerce is regulated by the **Ministry of Commerce**, which issued the **Digital Commerce Operation Guidelines in 2021** (after scandals such as Evaly). Trade body: **e-CAB** (e-Commerce Association of Bangladesh).

## E-governance (ই-গভর্ন্যান্স) 🔥
- **Using ICT to deliver government services and information** to citizens, businesses and other government bodies, making government **transparent, efficient and accountable**.
- **E-government** = digital delivery of services; **e-governance** is broader (includes citizen participation).

| Model | Meaning | Bangladesh example |
|---|---|---|
| 🔥 **G2C** (Government to Citizen) | Services to citizens | Online birth registration, e-passport, land records, **Union Digital Centres** |
| **G2B** (Government to Business) | Services to businesses | Online trade licence, **e-GP** tenders, online VAT/tax |
| **G2G** (Government to Government) | Between offices | **e-Nothi** (digital file system) |
| **G2E** (Government to Employee) | For government staff | Online pay fixation, iBAS++ (salary/budget system) |

### E-governance services in Bangladesh 🔥
| Service | Key fact |
|---|---|
| 🔥 **Union Digital Centre (UDC / ইউনিয়ন ডিজিটাল সেন্টার)** | One-stop service centres at every union; launched nationwide on **11 November 2010** (4,501 centres) |
| **a2i (Aspire to Innovate)** | Government programme (with UNDP support) behind many digital services |
| **National Portal** | **bangladesh.gov.bd** — tens of thousands of government office websites in one framework |
| 🔥 **999** | **National emergency service** (police, fire, ambulance), free; launched **2017** |
| **333** | **National call centre** for government information and services |
| **e-GP** | **Electronic Government Procurement**, run by **CPTU** (now the **Bangladesh Public Procurement Authority, BPPA**), started **2011** |
| **e-Return** | Online income-tax return (National Board of Revenue) |
| **NID / e-Passport** | E-passport launched **January 2020**; NID managed by the Election Commission |
| **Ekpay** | Single platform for paying utility bills |

- **Digital Bangladesh** was announced as a national vision in **December 2008** (target 2021). **12 December** has been observed as **Digital Bangladesh Day** (from 2017). A later vision, "Smart Bangladesh 2041", was announced in 2022.

> 🔄 Update: government programme names and rankings (e.g. the UN E-Government Development Index) change; check the latest news.

- M-commerce = via **mobile**; F-commerce = via **Facebook**.
- bKash **2011** (BRAC Bank); Rocket (Dutch-Bangla Bank); Nagad (Post Office, 2019).

- Union Digital Centres: **11 November 2010**.
- 999 = **national emergency service**; 333 = **national call centre**.
- e-GP = online government procurement (**2011**).

ICT-23.notes:
> **Why it matters:** Bangladesh-specific ICT facts are asked in almost every BCS and bank paper: the launch of Bangladesh's satellite, the landing stations of SEA-ME-WE 4 and 5, and the laws on cyber crime (ICT Act 2006 → Digital Security Act 2018 → Cyber Security Act 2023 → 2025 ordinance).

## Milestones of ICT in Bangladesh 🔥
| Event | Year / fact |
|---|---|
| **First computer** (IBM 1620, Atomic Energy Centre, Dhaka) | **1964** |
| First satellite earth station, **Betbunia (Rangamati)** | **1975** |
| **Bijoy** Bangla keyboard (Mustafa Jabbar) | **1988** |
| **Online internet** connection (via **VSAT**) | **1996** |
| **Bangladesh Telecommunication Regulatory Commission (BTRC)** formed under the Telecommunication Act 2001 | **2002** |
| First **submarine cable** (SEA-ME-WE 4) | **2006** |
| **Union Digital Centres** nationwide | **2010** |
| **4G** launched | **2018** |
| **Bangladesh's first satellite** launched | **May 2018** |
| **5G** trial (Teletalk) | **2021** |

## Bangladesh Satellite-1 (বাংলাদেশ স্যাটেলাইট-১) 🔥🔥
| Item | Fact |
|---|---|
| Former name | **Bangabandhu Satellite-1** (বঙ্গবন্ধু স্যাটেলাইট-১) |
| Type | **Geostationary communication satellite** — Bangladesh's **first** satellite |
| 🔥 Launch date | **12 May 2018** (Bangladesh time; it was still 11 May in the USA) |
| Launch site | **Kennedy Space Center, Florida, USA** |
| 🔥 Rocket / launcher | **SpaceX Falcon 9** (the first launch of the Block 5 version) |
| 🔥 Manufacturer | **Thales Alenia Space** (France–Italy) |
| 🔥 Orbital slot | **119.1° East** (bought from Russia's **Intersputnik**) |
| Transponders | **40**: **26 Ku-band + 14 C-band** |
| Ground stations | Main: **Gazipur**; backup: **Betbunia, Rangamati** |
| Operator | **Bangladesh Satellite Company Limited (BSCL)** |
| Expected life | About **15 years** |
| Uses | Direct-to-home (DTH) TV, TV channel broadcasting, internet and communication for remote areas, disaster communication |

- With this launch Bangladesh became the **57th country** to own a satellite (the figure most guides give).
- It was later renamed from "Bangabandhu Satellite-1" to "Bangladesh Satellite-1"; older guidebooks use the old name.

> 🔄 Update: check whether a second satellite project has been approved or launched.

## Submarine cables (সাবমেরিন ক্যাবল) 🔥🔥
Submarine cables are **optical fibre cables under the sea** that carry most international internet traffic. In Bangladesh they are run by **Bangladesh Submarine Cable PLC (BSCPLC)**, earlier **Bangladesh Submarine Cable Company Limited (BSCCL)**.

**SEA-ME-WE** = **South East Asia–Middle East–Western Europe**.

| Cable | Landing station | Connected |
|---|---|---|
| 🔥 **SEA-ME-WE 4** (1st cable) | **Cox's Bazar** (Jhilongja) | **2006** (21 May 2006) |
| 🔥 **SEA-ME-WE 5** (2nd cable) | **Kuakata, Patuakhali** | **2017** |
| **SEA-ME-WE 6** (3rd cable, under construction) | Cox's Bazar | Expected to be in service around 2025–26 |

- Memory hook: **4 → Cox's Bazar**, **5 → Kuakata**.
- Before 2006, Bangladesh used only **satellite (VSAT)** links for the internet.
- **ITC (International Terrestrial Cable):** licensed private companies (from **2012**) bring bandwidth over land from India, as a backup to submarine cables.

> 🔄 Update: check the latest status of SEA-ME-WE 6 and total bandwidth figures.

## Cyber and ICT laws of Bangladesh 🔥🔥
| Law | Key facts |
|---|---|
| **Bangladesh Telecommunication Act 2001** | Created **BTRC** (the telecom regulator) |
| 🔥 **ICT Act 2006** (তথ্য ও যোগাযোগ প্রযুক্তি আইন, ২০০৬) | First main cyber law; recognised **electronic records and digital signatures**; created the **Controller of Certifying Authorities (CCA)** and a **Cyber Tribunal**. Amended in **2013** (harsher punishment). Its **Section 57** (online defamation/"hurting religious sentiment") was heavily criticised |
| **Pornography Control Act 2012** | Punishes making and spreading pornography, including online |
| 🔥 **Digital Security Act 2018** (ডিজিটাল নিরাপত্তা আইন, ২০১৮) | Passed in **September 2018**; repealed Section 57 of the ICT Act (and related sections); created the **Digital Security Agency**. Widely criticised for curbing free speech |
| 🔥 **Cyber Security Act 2023** (সাইবার নিরাপত্তা আইন, ২০২৩) | Passed in **September 2023**; **replaced the Digital Security Act 2018**; the agency became the **National Cyber Security Agency (NCSA)**; reduced some punishments (e.g. many defamation offences made fine-only) |
| 🔥 **Cyber Security Ordinance 2025** (সাইবার সুরক্ষা অধ্যাদেশ, ২০২৫) | Issued by the **interim government** in **2025**; **replaced the Cyber Security Act 2023** and removed several speech-related offences |

- **Sequence to remember:** **ICT Act 2006 → Digital Security Act 2018 → Cyber Security Act 2023 → Cyber Security Ordinance 2025.**
- **BGD e-GOV CIRT** is the national Computer Incident Response Team.

> 🔄 Update: cyber laws were changed in 2025 and may be amended again (a parliament must pass or re-enact ordinances). Check the latest version and any data-protection law before the exam.

## Other bodies and facts
| Body / fact | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Bangladesh Computer Council (BCC)** | Government body for ICT development, under the **ICT Division** |
| **Bangladesh Hi-Tech Park Authority** | Develops hi-tech parks (e.g. Kaliakair, Gazipur; Jashore) |
| **National Data Centre** | **Tier IV**, Kaliakair, Gazipur |
| **Bangla ccTLD** | **.bd** and **.বাংলা** |
| **National ICT Policy** | Issued 2002, then **2009**, updated 2015 and **2018** |

- Orbital slot **119.1° E**; **40 transponders** (26 Ku + 14 C); main ground station **Gazipur**, backup **Betbunia**.

> **Why it matters:** Exams ask the elements of multimedia, lossy vs lossless formats, which extension belongs to which kind of file (.mp3, .avi, .apk, .pdf), RGB vs CMYK, and which software edits images, video or vector graphics.

## Multimedia (মাল্টিমিডিয়া) 🔥
- **Multimedia** means combining **two or more media** — **text, graphics/images, audio, video and animation** — usually with **interactivity**.
- Five elements: **Text, Image (graphics), Audio, Video, Animation**.
- Uses: education (e-learning), entertainment, advertising, presentations, games, virtual tours, **multimedia classrooms** (widely set up in Bangladeshi schools).
- **Hypermedia:** multimedia with **hyperlinks** (like the WWW).

## Images: raster vs vector 🔥
| Raster (bitmap) | Vector |
|---|---|
| Made of **pixels** | Made of **mathematical paths** (lines, curves) |
| **Loses quality (pixelates) when enlarged** | **No quality loss** when resized |
| Photos | Logos, icons, illustrations, maps |
| JPEG, PNG, GIF, BMP, TIFF | **SVG**, AI (Illustrator), EPS, **CDR** (CorelDRAW) |
| Edited in **Photoshop**, GIMP | Edited in **Illustrator**, **CorelDRAW**, Inkscape |

## Compression 🔥
- **Lossy compression:** removes some data permanently; much smaller files. **JPEG, MP3, MP4, AAC**.
- **Lossless compression:** no data lost; original can be restored exactly. **PNG, GIF, ZIP, RAR, FLAC**.
- **Codec** = **Co**der–**Dec**oder: software/hardware that compresses and decompresses audio/video (e.g. H.264).

## File formats (extensions) 🔥🔥
| Category | Extensions and facts |
|---|---|
| **Images** | **.jpg/.jpeg** (photos, lossy); **.png** (lossless, supports **transparency**); 🔥 **.gif** (**supports simple animation**, max **256 colours**); **.bmp** (Microsoft bitmap, uncompressed); **.tiff/.tif** (high quality, printing/scanning); **.svg** (vector, web); **.webp** (Google); **.ico** (icons); **.psd** (Photoshop project) |
| **Audio** | 🔥 **.mp3** (most popular, lossy); **.wav** (uncompressed, Microsoft/IBM); **.aac**; **.wma** (Windows Media Audio); **.flac** (lossless); **.ogg**; **.midi/.mid** (stores musical **instructions**, not recorded sound, so files are tiny) |
| **Video** | **.mp4** (MPEG-4, most common); **.avi** (Audio Video Interleave, **Microsoft**); **.mkv** (Matroska); **.mov** (**Apple QuickTime**); **.wmv** (Windows Media Video); **.flv** (Flash video); **.3gp** (old mobile phones); **.webm** (web) |
| **Documents** | **.txt** (plain text); **.docx/.doc** (Word); **.pdf** (Adobe, Portable Document Format); **.rtf** (Rich Text Format); **.odt** (OpenDocument text); **.xlsx**, **.pptx**, **.csv** |
| **Compressed / archive** | **.zip**, **.rar** (WinRAR), **.7z** (7-Zip), .tar, .gz |
| **Executable / installer** | 🔥 **.exe** (Windows program), .msi, **.bat** (batch file); **.apk** (**Android** app); **.ipa** (iOS app); **.dmg** (macOS disk image) |
| **Web** | **.html/.htm**, .css, .js, .php, .asp |
| **Programming** | .c, .cpp (C++), .java, .class (Java bytecode), .py (Python) |
| **Disk image** | **.iso** |

- **PDF** was created by **Adobe** (1993) and keeps the same layout on every device.

## Audio and video basics
- **Sampling rate:** samples of sound per second. **Audio CD quality = 44.1 kHz, 16-bit**, stereo.
- **Frame rate:** frames per second (**fps**); films are usually **24 fps**; the illusion of motion comes from **persistence of vision**.
- **Resolution:** **HD = 1280×720 (720p)**, **Full HD = 1920×1080 (1080p)**, **4K UHD = 3840×2160**.
- **Aspect ratio:** width : height, e.g. **16:9** (widescreen) or 4:3.
- **Streaming:** playing audio/video while it downloads (YouTube, Netflix, Spotify).
- **Podcast:** audio (or video) shows released in episodes online.

## Colour models 🔥
| Model | Colours | Used for |
|---|---|---|
| 🔥 **RGB** | **Red, Green, Blue** (**additive**: all three together = white) | **Screens**: monitors, TVs, phones, cameras |
| 🔥 **CMYK** | **Cyan, Magenta, Yellow, Key (Black)** (**subtractive**) | **Printing** |

- 24-bit colour ("true colour") can show about **16.7 million** colours (2²⁴).

## Animation
- **2D animation**, **3D animation** (Blender, Maya), **stop-motion**.
- **Tweening (in-betweening):** creating frames between two key frames automatically.
- 🔥 **Morphing:** smoothly **changing one image into another**.
- **Adobe Flash** was widely used for web animation; Adobe **ended Flash support in 2020**.

- Raster = **pixels**; vector = **paths**, scales without loss (**SVG, AI, CDR**).

- **GIF** supports animation, 256 colours; **PNG** supports transparency.
